topic.title: PSA: bf16 on Kaggle's T4/P100 silently cost me 0.14 AUC (0.851 → 0.710). How to spot it.

comments.content:
Great write-up. "A silent partial fallback looks exactly like a bad model" is the line I wish I'd read earlier. Two related things that only showed up at hidden-test scale for us:

  • If you push kernels with the CLI, set "machine_shape": "NvidiaTeslaT4" in kernel-metadata.json. Otherwise a GPU kernel can land on a P100 (sm_60), which the offline torch build we used doesn't support.
  • For blend kernels with a try/except fallback, check the commit log for each member's fallback/empty count, not just that submission.csv exists. A member that fails quietly still produces a perfectly valid-looking file.

Thanks for sharing your DINOv2 approach. Would you consider publicly releasing the five-fold checkpoints and a minimal inference/preprocessing script for all participants? An independent architecture would be valuable to evaluate before the final deadline. A public download link with the required settings and license would be very helpful.
Good catch! You need to use torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(including_emulation=False) though as the default may still output true depending on torch version.

Hi, I’m interested in teaming up before the merger deadline. I currently have a 0.944 reproducible ensemble and I’m in discussions with a 0.963 competitor about merging. Your independent DINOv2 arm sounds highly complementary. Are you still open to a team merge?
As far as I understand, the P100 and T4 GPUs do not support bfloat16.
